The second: that it is not connected to it, and the meaning is: they are bound together and fettered. The share of reason in this is known from what has been indicated earlier.

The second attribute: His saying: ﴿Their garments of pitch﴾. "Sarabil" is the plural of "sirbal," which is the shirt. "Qatiran" has three dialectal forms: qatran, qitran, and qatiran, with the qaf vowelled with fatha or kasra and the ta' sukun, or with fatha on the qaf and kasra on the ta'. It is a substance that exudes from a tree called al-abhal; it is boiled and smeared on mangy camels, and by its heat and sharpness it burns off the mange. Its heat may reach into the interior of the body. Its nature is that fire spreads quickly in it, and it is black in color and foul in smell. The skins of the people of Hell are smeared with it until that smearing becomes like garments, which are shirts. Four kinds of punishment result from them: the sting and burning of the pitch, the rapid spread of the fire over their skins, the black color, and the stench of the smell. Also, the difference between the pitch of the Resurrection and the pitch of this world is like the difference between the two fires. I say: the share of reason in this is that the substance of the spirit is a luminous, shining substance from the world of holiness and the absence of majesty, and this body functions as a garment and shirt for it. Everything that befalls the soul of pains and griefs happens only because of this body. Therefore there is a sting and burning in the substance of the soul because of this body, since desire, greed, and anger spread quickly to the substance of the spirit through it. Its being dense, murky, and dark is what hides the shine and light of the spirit, and it is the cause of foulness and putrefaction. So this body resembles garments of pitch and tar. Some read: "from qitrin ani," and "qitr" is molten copper or brass, and "ani" is that whose heat has reached its extreme. Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari said: That fire does not destroy that pitch nor annihilate it, just as the fire does not destroy their bodies or the shackles that were upon them.

The third attribute: His saying: ﴿and fire covers their faces﴾. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Is one who shields his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]?﴾ [al-Zumar: 24], and His saying: ﴿The Day they will be dragged into the Fire on their faces﴾ [al-Qamar: 48].

Know that the locus of knowledge and ignorance, of definiteness and indefiniteness, is the heart, and the locus of thought, illusion, and imagination is

The head (al-ra's). The effects of these states appear primarily in the face, so for this reason God Most High singled out these two organs for the manifestation of the signs of punishment. Regarding the heart, He said: ﴿The fire of God, kindled﴾, ﴿which mounts over the hearts﴾ [al-Humazah 104:6–7]. Regarding the face, He said: ﴿and the Fire will cover their faces﴾, with the meaning of "will envelop." When God Most High mentioned these three attributes, He said: ﴿That God may recompense every soul for what it has earned﴾. Al-Wahidi said: "What is meant by this is the souls of the disbelievers, because what was mentioned before does not befit being a recompense for the people of faith." I say: It is possible to keep the word on its general meaning, because the wording of the verse indicates that God Most High recompenses every person with what befits his deed and earnings. Since the earnings of these disbelievers are disbelief and disobedience, their recompense is this punishment that has been mentioned. Since the earnings of the believers are faith and obedience, what befits them is reward. Also, since God Most High punishes the guilty for their crime, it is all the more fitting that He rewards the obedient for their obedience.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, God is swift in reckoning﴾. What is meant is that God Most High does not wrong them, nor does He add to the punishment they deserve. As for the share of reason in this: the dark moral qualities are the origins of the occurrence of spiritual pains, and the presence of those qualities in the soul is in proportion to the issuing of those actions from them in the worldly life. This is because the psychic dispositions (al-malakat al-nafsaniyyah) come into being in the essence of the soul through repeated actions. On this assumption, those pains vary according to those actions in their multiplicity and fewness, their intensity and weakness, and that resembles reckoning.

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿This is a message for mankind﴾, meaning: this admonition and exhortation is a message for mankind, that is, a sufficiency in exhortation. Then they differed: it was said that His saying "this" refers to the entire Qur'an; it was said, rather, that it refers to this entire surah; and it was said, rather, that it refers to what is mentioned from His saying ﴿And do not think﴾ to His saying ﴿swift in reckoning﴾. As for His saying ﴿and that they may be warned thereby﴾, it is coordinated with an omitted element, meaning: so that they may take advice; ﴿and that they may be warned thereby﴾, that is, by this message.

Then He said: ﴿and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: We have mentioned in this book many times that the human soul has two branches: the theoretical faculty (al-quwwah al-nazariyyah), whose perfection lies in knowing existing things according to their categories, genera and species, until the soul becomes like a mirror in which the holiness of the dominion (al-malakut) is reflected and in which the majesty of divinity (al-lahut) appears. The head of these knowledges and this illumination is knowledge of the oneness of God according to His essence, attributes and actions.

The second branch: the practical faculty (al-quwwah al-'amaliyyah), whose happiness lies in its becoming characterized by virtuous morals, which become the origins for the issuing of perfect actions from it. The head of the happinesses of this faculty is obedience to God and service to Him.

Having understood this, we say: His saying ﴿that they may know that He is but one God﴾ is an indication of what functions as the head for the perfection of the state of the theoretical faculty, and His saying ﴿and that those of understanding may take heed﴾ is an indication of what functions as the head for the perfection of the state of the practical faculty. The benefit of this remembrance is nothing but turning away from vain actions and turning toward righteous actions. This conclusion is like a decisive proof that there is no happiness for man except through these two aspects.

The second issue: These verses indicate that reminding with these admonitions and advices necessitates standing upon the oneness of God and turning to righteous action. The reason is that when a person hears these frightening warnings and cautions, his fear grows and he occupies himself with reflection and contemplation, so he reaches knowledge of the oneness of God and prophethood, and occupies himself with righteous deeds.

[p. 119]

The third issue: The Qadi said: The beginning and end of this surah indicate that the servant is independent in his action: if he wills, he obeys, and if he wills, he disobeys. As for the beginning of this surah, it is His saying: ﴿that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into light﴾ [Ibrahim 14:1]. We have mentioned there that this indicates that the purpose of sending down the Book is to guide all creatures to the religion and piety and to prevent them from disbelief and disobedience. As for the end of the surah, His saying ﴿and that those of understanding may take heed﴾ indicates that God Most High sent down this surah, and mentioned these advices and admonitions, only so that creatures may benefit from them, so they become believers and obedient, and abandon disbelief and disobedience. So it becomes clear that the beginning and end of this surah agree in conveying this meaning. Know that the thorough answer to this is mentioned at the beginning of the surah, so there is no benefit in repeating it.

The fourth issue: This verse indicates that there is no excellence for man and no merit for him except through his intellect, because God Most High explained that He sent down these books and sent the messengers only to remind those of understanding. Were it not for the great nobility and the lofty rank of those of understanding, the matter would not be so.

The author, may God have mercy on him and be pleased with him, said: The commentary on this surah was completed on Friday, at the end of Sha'ban in the year six hundred and one, and it was concluded with goodness and forgiveness in the desert of Baghdad. We ask God for deliverance from griefs and sorrows, success in attaining the degrees of Paradise, and deliverance from the levels of the Fire; indeed He is the King, the Bestower, the Merciful, the Judge of Recompense. By the praise of God and the goodness of His success. May His blessings and peace be upon the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad, and his family, and may He grant them peace.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 14, verses 47–52 (part 1 of 2):

The words of the Exalted: ﴿So do not think that Allah would break His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Almighty, Owner of Retribution.﴾

Know that in the first verse He said: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do﴾ [Ibrahim: 42], and in this verse He said: ﴿So do not think that Allah would break His promise to His messengers.﴾ The purpose of this is to point out that if Allah did not establish the Resurrection and did not take retribution on behalf of the oppressed from the oppressors, it would necessarily follow either that He is unaware, or that He breaks His promise. Since it is established in sound minds that both of these are impossible, the claim that He does not establish the Resurrection is false. His words ﴿breaking His promise to His messengers﴾ refer to His saying: ﴿Indeed, We shall surely help Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 51], and His saying: ﴿Allah has decreed: "Surely I shall prevail, and My messengers."﴾ [al-Mujadila: 21].

If it is said: Why was it not said "breaking His messengers' promise," and why was the second object placed before the first?

We say: So that it would be known that He does not break promises at all, for Allah does not break the appointed time. Then He said ﴿His messengers﴾ to indicate that since He does not break His promise to anyone, and it is not part of His nature to break promises, how could He break them to His messengers, who are His chosen ones and His elite? It was also read as "breaking the promise of His messengers" with the word "messengers" in the genitive and "promise" in the accusative, the implied construction being "breaking His messengers' promise." This reading is weak, like the one who reads "the killing of their children of their partners" [al-An'am: 137]. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Almighty﴾, i.e., Overpowering, who cannot be outwitted, ﴿Owner of Retribution﴾ against His allies.

﴿On the day when the earth will be changed into a different earth, and the heavens as well, and they will come out before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾. ﴿And you will see the criminals that day bound together in shackles﴾. ﴿Their garments of pitch, and fire covering their faces﴾. ﴿That Allah may recompense every soul for what it has earned. Indeed, Allah is swift in reckoning.﴾ ﴿This is a message for mankind, that they may be warned by it, and that they may know that He is but one God, and that people of understanding may take heed.﴾

Know that when Allah said ﴿Almighty, Owner of Retribution﴾, He explained the time of His retribution, saying ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed into a different earth﴾, and He magnified the state of that day, because there is no matter greater in minds and souls than the change of the heavens and the earth. In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: al-Zajjaj mentioned two possibilities regarding the accusative of "the day" (yawma): either it is an adverbial complement of "retribution," or it is a substitute for His saying ﴿the day when the punishment comes to them﴾.

The second issue: Know that "tabdil" (change/replacement) may have two meanings:

One: that the essence remains and its attribute is changed into another attribute.

Two: that the first essence perishes and another essence comes into being. The evidence that the mention of the word "tabdil" may be intended to mean a change of attribute is permissible is that one says: "I changed the ring into a seal" (badhdhaltu al-halqata khatiman) when you melt it and shape it into a seal, moving it from one form to another. From this is His saying: ﴿Those, Allah will change their evil deeds into good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70]. One also says: "I changed my shirt into a robe," meaning I moved the substance from one attribute to another attribute. One also says: "Zayd changed (tabaddala)" when his conditions have altered. As for the mention of the word "tabdil" when change occurs in essences, it is like your saying: "I changed the dirhams into dinars." From this is His saying: ﴿We changed them, [giving them] other skins﴾ [al-Nisa': 56], and His saying: ﴿And We changed their two gardens into two gardens﴾ [Saba': 16]. When you know that the word is capable of both of these meanings, there are two views concerning the verse:

The first view: that what is meant is the change of attribute, not the change of essence. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "It is that same earth, but it has changed in its attributes. Its mountains are removed from it, its seas are made to burst forth, and it is leveled, so that no crookedness or elevation is seen in it." Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "Allah will change the earth into another earth, spreading it out and stretching it like a leather hide of 'Ukaz; you will see no crookedness or elevation in it." His words ﴿and the heavens﴾ mean that the heavens will be changed into other heavens, similar to his saying, peace be upon him: "A believer is not to be killed for a disbeliever, nor one who has a covenant during his covenant." The meaning is: nor one who has a covenant during his covenant is to be killed for a disbeliever. The change of the heavens is by the scattering of their stars and their splitting apart, the folding up of their sun, the eclipse of their moon, their becoming gates, and that at times they will be like molten metal and at times like red leather.

The second view: that what is meant is the change of essence. Ibn Mas'ud said: "It will be replaced by an earth like white silver, pure, on which no blood has been shed and no sin has been committed." This is the explanation of these two views. Some people preferred the first view, saying: Because His saying ﴿the day when the earth will be changed﴾ means this earth, and "change" is an attribute attached to it, and when an attribute exists, the thing described must exist. Since the thing described by change is this earth, it must be that this earth remains at the time of that change. It is impossible for this earth to remain with its attributes at the time of that change, for otherwise change would be impossible. Therefore what remains must be the essence. Thus it is established that this verse requires the essence to remain. Those who hold this view are the ones who say that at the establishment of the Resurrection Allah does not annihilate the essences and bodies, but only annihilates their attributes and states.

Know that it is not far-fetched to say that what is meant by the change of the earth and the heavens is that He will make the earth Hell and make the heavens Paradise. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in 'Illiyyun﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 18], and His saying: ﴿No! Indeed, the record of the wicked is in Sijjin﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 7]. And Allah knows best.

As for His saying: ﴿and they will come out before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾, we say: As for "coming out before Allah," we have explained it in His saying: ﴿And they will all come out before Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 21]. He mentioned "the One, the Subduer" here because when the dominion belongs to one sole owner who is overpowering and cannot be overcome, and Subduer who cannot be conquered, no one has any refuge other than Him, and the matter becomes extremely severe. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is Allah's, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. When He described Himself, glorified be He, as Subduer, He demonstrated their helplessness and humiliation, saying: ﴿And you will see the criminals on that day﴾.

* * *

Know that He, the Exalted, mentioned among the attributes of their helplessness and humiliation several matters:

The first attribute: that they are bound together in shackles. It is said: "I tied a thing to another thing" when you bound it to it and joined it. "Qiran" is the name of the rope with which two things are tied. Here it came in the intensive form because of the large number of those people. "Al-asfad" is the plural of "safad," which is the shackle.

Having known this, we say: concerning His saying ﴿bound together﴾ there are three aspects:

One of them: al-Kalbi said: "Bound together" means every disbeliever together with a devil in a chain. 'Ata' said: this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And when souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir: 7], i.e., joined together, so Allah joins the souls of believers with the wide-eyed houris, and the souls of disbelievers with their companions among the devils. I say: the share of rational inquiry in this is that when a human being departs from this world, either he has trained his soul, refined it, and called it to knowledge of Allah, obedience to Him, and love of Him, or he has not done so, but has left it immersed in bodily pleasures and occupied with imaginary and fanciful conditions. If it is the first, that soul departs toward the divine presence and happiness through the eternal grace. If it is the second, that soul departs with regret, sorrow, and severe affliction, because of its inclination toward the world of body. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And when souls are paired﴾ [al-Takwir: 7]. The devil of the disbelieving soul is the false dispositions and corrupt events, and this is what 'Ata' meant when he said that every disbeliever is bound together in shackles with his devil.

The second view in interpreting His saying ﴿bound together in shackles﴾ is that some disbelievers are joined to others. What is meant is that those wretched souls and turbid, darkened spirits, because they are alike and similar, join one another, and the darkness of each one calls out to the other. The descent of each one of them to the other in those darknesses and losses is what is meant by His saying: ﴿bound together in shackles﴾.

The third view: Zayd ibn Arqam said: their hands and feet are drawn up to their necks with iron collars. The share of reason in this is that the dispositions that arise in the substance of the soul are produced only by repeated actions performed by the limbs and organs. When those dispositions are dark and turbid, it is as though their hands and feet were bound and fettered to their necks. As for His saying ﴿in shackles﴾, there are two aspects:

One: that this is connected to ﴿bound together﴾, and the meaning is: they are bound together with shackles.

The second: that it is not connected to it, and the meaning is: they are bound together and fettered. The share of reason in this is known from what has been indicated earlier.

The second attribute: His saying: ﴿Their garments of pitch﴾. "Sarabil" is the plural of "sirbal," which is the shirt. "Qatiran" has three dialectal forms: qatran, qitran, and qatiran, with the qaf vowelled with fatha or kasra and the ta' sukun, or with fatha on the qaf and kasra on the ta'. Its heat may reach into the interior of the body. Its nature is that fire spreads quickly in it, and it is black in color and foul in smell. The skins of the people of Hell are smeared with it until that smearing becomes like garments, which are shirts. Four kinds of punishment result from them: the sting and burning of the pitch, the rapid spread of the fire over their skins, the black color, and the stench of the smell. Also, the difference between the pitch of the Resurrection and the pitch of this world is like the difference between the two fires. I say: the share of reason in this is that the substance of the spirit is a luminous, shining substance from the world of holiness and the absence of majesty, and this body functions as a garment and shirt for it. Everything that befalls the soul of pains and griefs happens only because of this body. Therefore there is a sting and burning in the substance of the soul because of this body, since desire, greed, and anger spread quickly to the substance of the spirit through it. Its being dense, murky, and dark is what hides the shine and light of the spirit, and it is the cause of foulness and putrefaction. So this body resembles garments of pitch and tar. Some read: "from qitrin ani," and "qitr" is molten copper or brass, and "ani" is that whose heat has reached its extreme. Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari said: That fire does not destroy that pitch nor annihilate it, just as the fire does not destroy their bodies or the shackles that were upon them.

The third attribute: His saying: ﴿and fire covers their faces﴾. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Is one who shields his face from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one who is safe]?﴾ [al-Zumar: 24], and His saying: ﴿The Day they will be dragged into the Fire on their faces﴾ [al-Qamar: 48].

Know that the locus of knowledge and ignorance, of definiteness and indefiniteness, is the heart, and the locus of thought, illusion, and imagination is

The head (al-ra's). The effects of these states appear primarily in the face, so for this reason God Most High singled out these two organs for the manifestation of the signs of punishment. Regarding the heart, He said: ﴿The fire of God, kindled﴾, ﴿which mounts over the hearts﴾ [al-Humazah 104:6–7]. Regarding the face, He said: ﴿and the Fire will cover their faces﴾, with the meaning of "will envelop." When God Most High mentioned these three attributes, He said: ﴿That God may recompense every soul for what it has earned﴾. Al-Wahidi said: "What is meant by this is the souls of the disbelievers, because what was mentioned before does not befit being a recompense for the people of faith." I say: It is possible to keep the word on its general meaning, because the wording of the verse indicates that God Most High recompenses every person with what befits his deed and earnings. Since the earnings of these disbelievers are disbelief and disobedience, their recompense is this punishment that has been mentioned. Since the earnings of the believers are faith and obedience, what befits them is reward. Also, since God Most High punishes the guilty for their crime, it is all the more fitting that He rewards the obedient for their obedience.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, God is swift in reckoning﴾. What is meant is that God Most High does not wrong them, nor does He add to the punishment they deserve. As for the share of reason in this: the dark moral qualities are the origins of the occurrence of spiritual pains, and the presence of those qualities in the soul is in proportion to the issuing of those actions from them in the worldly life. This is because the psychic dispositions (al-malakat al-nafsaniyyah) come into being in the essence of the soul through repeated actions. On this assumption, those pains vary according to those actions in their multiplicity and fewness, their intensity and weakness, and that resembles reckoning.

* * *

Then God Most High said: ﴿This is a message for mankind﴾, meaning: this admonition and exhortation is a message for mankind, that is, a sufficiency in exhortation. Then they differed: it was said that His saying "this" refers to the entire Qur'an; it was said, rather, that it refers to this entire surah; and it was said, rather, that it refers to what is mentioned from His saying ﴿And do not think﴾ to His saying ﴿swift in reckoning﴾. As for His saying ﴿and that they may be warned thereby﴾, it is coordinated with an omitted element, meaning: so that they may take advice; ﴿and that they may be warned thereby﴾, that is, by this message.

Then He said: ﴿and that they may know that He is but one God, and that those of understanding may take heed﴾. Concerning this there are several issues:

The first issue: We have mentioned in this book many times that the human soul has two branches: the theoretical faculty (al-quwwah al-nazariyyah), whose perfection lies in knowing existing things according to their categories, genera and species, until the soul becomes like a mirror in which the holiness of the dominion (al-malakut) is reflected and in which the majesty of divinity (al-lahut) appears. Having understood this, we say: His saying ﴿that they may know that He is but one God﴾ is an indication of what functions as the head for the perfection of the state of the theoretical faculty, and His saying ﴿and that those of understanding may take heed﴾ is an indication of what functions as the head for the perfection of the state of the practical faculty. The benefit of this remembrance is nothing but turning away from vain actions and turning toward righteous actions. This conclusion is like a decisive proof that there is no happiness for man except through these two aspects.

The second issue: These verses indicate that reminding with these admonitions and advices necessitates standing upon the oneness of God and turning to righteous action. The reason is that when a person hears these frightening warnings and cautions, his fear grows and he occupies himself with reflection and contemplation, so he reaches knowledge of the oneness of God and prophethood, and occupies himself with righteous deeds.

[p. 119]

The third issue: The Qadi said: The beginning and end of this surah indicate that the servant is independent in his action: if he wills, he obeys, and if he wills, he disobeys. As for the beginning of this surah, it is His saying: ﴿that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into light﴾ [Ibrahim 14:1]. We have mentioned there that this indicates that the purpose of sending down the Book is to guide all creatures to the religion and piety and to prevent them from disbelief and disobedience. As for the end of the surah, His saying ﴿and that those of understanding may take heed﴾ indicates that God Most High sent down this surah, and mentioned these advices and admonitions, only so that creatures may benefit from them, so they become believers and obedient, and abandon disbelief and disobedience. So it becomes clear that the beginning and end of this surah agree in conveying this meaning. Know that the thorough answer to this is mentioned at the beginning of the surah, so there is no benefit in repeating it.

The fourth issue: This verse indicates that there is no excellence for man and no merit for him except through his intellect, because God Most High explained that He sent down these books and sent the messengers only to remind those of understanding. Were it not for the great nobility and the lofty rank of those of understanding, the matter would not be so.

The author, may God have mercy on him and be pleased with him, said: The commentary on this surah was completed on Friday, at the end of Sha'ban in the year six hundred and one, and it was concluded with goodness and forgiveness in the desert of Baghdad. We ask God for deliverance from griefs and sorrows, success in attaining the degrees of Paradise, and deliverance from the levels of the Fire; indeed He is the King, the Bestower, the Merciful, the Judge of Recompense. By the praise of God and the goodness of His success. May His blessings and peace be upon the Seal of the Prophets, Muhammad, and his family, and may He grant them peace.
